instruction.text: This is a map of Southern South America. Select the cactus to learn more.
This is the Atacama Desert in northern Chile. Listen and select the correct description.

hint.text: Some parts of the desert haven’t received a single drop of rain for hundreds of years!
hint.label: Did you know?

b.sound: The Atacama Desert is the driest non-polar place on Earth.
The Atacama Desert is the driest polar place on Earth.
Its landscape is often compared to the Moon or the planet Mars.
Its landscape is often compared to the Amazon Rainforest.
It is one of the best places in the world to observe stars.
It is one of the best places in the world to observe aeroplanes.
Many animals such as flamingos have adapted to survive in its extremely dry climate.
The climate is too hot for any animals to survive.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: The Pampas are vast, continuous grassland plains that cover all of Uruguay and large parts of northern Argentina.
The mineral-rich, fertile soil makes it one of Earth’s most important farming regions, producing huge amounts of wheat, corn and grains.
Expert horsemen called gauchos have roamed the plains for centuries, herding cattle, sheep and horses.
The Pampas are home to many interesting animals, including deer, wolves, pumas and rheas — a large flightless bird.

hint.label: Seven Summits
hint.text:
The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent:

1. Mount Everest (Asia) - 8,849 m
2. Aconcagua (South America) - 6,961 m
3. Denali (North America) - 6,194 m
4. Mount Kilimanjaro (Africa) - 5,895 m
5. Mount Elbrus (Europe) - 5,642 m
6. Mount Vinson (Antarctica) - 4,892 m
7. Mount Kosciuszko (Australia) - 2,228 m
hint.sound: The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent.

atoms.b: Argentina’s Aconcagua is the ((hottest ++tallest)) mountain in South America and, therefore, one of the Seven Summits.
atoms.sound: Argentina’s Acon kagwa is the tallest mountain in South America and, therefore, one of the Seven Summits.

atoms.b: At nearly 7,000 m above sea level, it is also the tallest mountain on ((Europe ++Earth)) outside of Asia.
Aconcagua was once an active ((lake ++volcano)) and is one of hundreds that have shaped the climate and landscape of the Andes over thousands of years.
atoms.sound: Acon kagwa was once an active volcano and is one of hundreds that have shaped the climate and landscape of the Andes over thousands of years.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Covering all of southern Chile and Argentina, the region of Patagonia is one of the most remote and wild places on Earth.
Western Patagonia is dominated by the Andes, where ancient rivers and glaciers have carved out deep fjords and mountains over thousands of years, such as in Los Glaciares National Park.
The Patagonian Steppe covers the central and eastern regions, from the Andes to the Atlantic coast. It is an example of a cold desert grassland, where the climate is extremely cold, windy and dry.
In the southernmost part of Patagonia, you can find the isolated archipelago of Tierra del Fuego. The city of Ushuaia is located here and is Earth’s southernmost city.
atoms.sound: In the southernmost part of Patagonia, you can find the isolated arkapelligo of Tierra del Fuego. The city of Ushuaia is located here and is Earth’s southernmost city.

hint.label: Archipelago
hint.text: An archipelago is a group or chain of islands.
hint.sound: An arkapelligo is a group or chain of islands.
